title: orders-api database connection pool exhausted
root_cause: Database connection pool exhaustion caused by a new N+1 enrichment query holding connections longer
resolution: Rolled back v4.2.0, raised orders-api DB pool from 30 to 45 and restarted API pods
engineer_notes: Postgres itself was healthy (CPU 34%). The bottleneck was the application-side pool.

title: checkout-web blank payment step after config deploy
root_cause: Bad deployment configuration: PAYMENT_API_BASE_URL pointed to a non-existent /api/v2 path
resolution: Rolled back to v9.13.2; added config validation to the deploy pipeline
engineer_notes: Config-only deploys still need a canary.

title: payment-api Redis connection pool exhaustion
root_cause: Redis connection pool exhaustion in the payment-api application (client-side pool too small for new rate-limit lookups)
resolution: Increased payment-api Redis connection pool from 20 to 40 and restarted API workers. Latency and errors returned to baseline within 4 minutes.
engineer_notes: Redis server was healthy (CPU 18%, memory 37%). Restarting Redis was not required.

title: payment-api charge latency from PayFlow provider
root_cause: External payment provider (PayFlow) latency degradation in eu-west region
resolution: Enabled circuit breaker and failed over card charges to secondary provider (CardStream) until PayFlow recovered
engineer_notes: Check provider status page and upstream latency before scaling ourselves.

title: inventory-service OOMKilled pods
root_cause: Memory leak in unbounded in-process SKU cache
resolution: Added LRU bound (50k entries) to cache; rolling restart
engineer_notes: Raising limits hides leaks. Look at heap growth slope.

title: orders-api pool exhaustion during batch export
symptoms: nightly export job running during business hours
root_cause: Database connection pool exhaustion: export job shared the API connection pool
resolution: Paused export job, moved it to a dedicated pool of 10 connections
engineer_notes: Batch jobs must never share the request-serving pool.

title: session-service Redis server memory saturation
symptoms: Redis used_memory at maxmemory with 12k evictions/sec
root_cause: Redis server itself unhealthy: memory saturation and eviction storm after session TTL increase
resolution: Failed over to Redis replica and restarted the primary, reverted TTL to 1h, scaled Redis memory
engineer_notes: Here restarting/failing over Redis WAS correct because the Redis server itself was unhealthy (CPU 97%, maxmemory, evictions). Client pool was NOT saturated (18/50).

title: notification-service emails stopped after config deploy
root_cause: Bad deployment configuration: consumers subscribed to a renamed queue that producers did not use
resolution: Rolled back queue name config; redeployed

failed_approaches.result: No effect - wrong queue name persisted

engineer_notes: Silent config mismatches: compare producer and consumer config.

title: payment-api PayFlow timeouts during peak
root_cause: External payment provider latency (PayFlow regional degradation)
resolution: Circuit breaker opened, charges routed to CardStream; recovered after provider fix
engineer_notes: Redis pool normal - not a Redis issue.

title: search-api latency creep and OOM
root_cause: Memory leak from event listeners never unregistered in query analytics
resolution: Hotfix v7.2.1 unregistering listeners; rolling restart

title: payment-api Redis timeout cascade

recent_deployment.change: Added Redis session lookup to payment authorization

root_cause: Redis connection pool exhaustion in payment-api (application-side pool saturated by new session lookups)
resolution: Increased payment-api Redis connection pool from 40 to 60 and restarted API workers. Recovered in 5 minutes.

failed_approaches.result: Incident persisted; outage extended by 25 minutes and reconnect storm briefly increased errors to 34%

engineer_notes: Restarting Redis was the wrong call - Redis server was healthy (CPU 24%). The bottleneck was the application connection pool.

title: orders-api connection leak
root_cause: Database connection pool exhaustion from a connection leak in the exception path
resolution: Rolled back v4.5.0 and restarted API pods to release leaked connections

failed_approaches.action: Failed over Postgres primary to replica
failed_approaches.result: No effect - database was healthy; added 6 minutes of write downtime

engineer_notes: Do not fail over the database when the database is healthy and only the app pool is exhausted.

title: payment-api upstream timeout misconfiguration
symptoms: error rate spike immediately after deploy
root_cause: Bad deployment configuration: provider timeout set to 500ms (typo)
resolution: Rolled back to v2.5.3
engineer_notes: Errors at a suspiciously exact latency = timeout config.

title: payment-api PayFlow 3DS latency
root_cause: External payment provider latency on 3DS service
resolution: Waited for provider fix; enabled async 3DS confirmation

title: inventory-service leak in websocket handler
symptoms: memory grows with websocket connection count
root_cause: Memory leak: websocket subscriptions retained after disconnect
resolution: Hotfix to clean up subscriptions on disconnect

title: user-service pool exhaustion

recent_deployment.change: Added audit log write per login

root_cause: Database connection pool exhaustion from synchronous audit writes
resolution: Made audit writes async; increased pool to 35; restarted pods

title: payment-api pointed at PayFlow sandbox
symptoms: 100% of live charges rejected with 401 from provider
root_cause: Bad deployment configuration: PAYFLOW_API_URL pointed to sandbox environment
resolution: Rolled back to v2.7.0 within 9 minutes
engineer_notes: Provider 401s right after a config deploy - roll back first.

title: search-api leak in query cache
root_cause: Memory leak: unbounded query cache
resolution: Bounded cache with TTL; rolling restart

title: payment-api connection saturation after fraud cache

recent_deployment.change: Added Redis fraud-score cache lookup per charge

root_cause: Redis connection pool exhaustion in payment-api: the new per-charge fraud cache lookup increased connection demand beyond the pool size
resolution: Increased payment-api Redis connection pool from 60 to 100 and restarted API workers. Recovered in 6 minutes.
engineer_notes: Same failure signature as INC-003 and INC-011. On-call considered restarting Redis but Redis server health was normal (CPU 27%) so it was skipped, per INC-011.

title: orders-api pool exhaustion from slow query
root_cause: Database connection pool exhaustion caused by a missing index on a new reporting query
resolution: Added index; disabled reporting endpoint temporarily

title: notification-service SMS provider latency
root_cause: External SMS provider latency
resolution: Failed over to secondary SMS provider

title: checkout-web feature flag misconfiguration
symptoms: new checkout flow enabled for 100% instead of 5%
root_cause: Bad deployment configuration: feature flag percentage set to 100
resolution: Set flag back to 5% and rolled back

title: inventory-service leak from metrics labels
root_cause: Memory leak due to unbounded metric label cardinality
resolution: Removed SKU label; rolling restart

title: payment-api Redis pool exhaustion during flash sale
root_cause: Redis connection pool exhaustion in payment-api under 3x flash-sale traffic
resolution: Temporarily increased payment-api Redis connection pool from 100 to 150 and restarted API workers; reverted to 100 after the sale. Recovered in 4 minutes.
engineer_notes: Same remediation pattern as INC-003/INC-011/INC-019. Redis server healthy. Action item: permanent pool sizing review (not yet done).

title: orders-api pool exhaustion after worker scale-up
root_cause: Database connection exhaustion: pods x pool size exceeded Postgres max_connections
resolution: Introduced PgBouncer, reduced per-pod pool

title: payment-api PayFlow regional outage
root_cause: External payment provider outage (PayFlow)
resolution: Circuit breaker + failover to CardStream
engineer_notes: Distinguish provider latency (upstream high, Redis pool normal) from Redis pool exhaustion (pool at capacity).
